question: to the Commission Tamás Deutsch (PfE), Kinga Gál (PfE), Mieke Andriese (PfE), Gerolf Annemans (PfE), Paolo Borchia (PfE), Mireia Borrás Pabón (PfE), Irmhild Boßdorf (ESN), Zsuzsanna Borvendég (ESN), Anna Bryłka (PfE), Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE), Petr Bystron (ESN), Margarita de la Pisa Carrión (PfE), Elisabeth Dieringer (PfE), Csaba Dömötör (PfE), Viktória Ferenc (PfE), Carlo Fidanza (ECR), Juan Carlos Girauta Vidal (PfE), Enikő Győri (PfE), András Gyürk (PfE), Roman Haider (PfE), György Hölvényi (PfE), Paolo Inselvini (ECR), Patryk Jaki (ECR), Alexander Jungbluth (ESN), Ondřej Knotek (PfE), Sebastian Kruis (PfE), András László (PfE), Afroditi Latinopoulou (PfE), Jorge Martín Frías (PfE), Georg Mayer (PfE), Tiago Moreira de Sá (PfE), Jana Nagyová (PfE), Jacek Ozdoba (ECR), Gilles Pennelle (PfE), Ernő Schaller-Baross (PfE), Antonín Staněk (PfE), Petra Steger (PfE), Pál Szekeres (PfE), António Tânger Corrêa (PfE), Hermann Tertsch (PfE), Tom Vandendriessche (PfE), Harald Vilimsky (PfE), Auke Zijlstra (PfE) Subject:

On 22 June 2026, Péter Magyar’s government submitted a proposal for the 17th amendment to the Fundamental Law.1 The proposed changes violate the most fundamental democratic and constitutional principles. Unprecedented in Europe, the changes would remove with immediate effect the legitimately elected President of the Republic years before the end of his term through ad hominem legislation. The proposal also restricts citizens’ electoral rights by forbidding anyone who has previously served as a member of the National Assembly for at least 12 years from running as a candidate in elections. The proposal also terminates the mandates of all Constitutional Court members who have reached the age of 70. This constitutes retroactive and ad hominem legislation, resulting in the early termination of four constitutional judges’ mandates, including the President of the Constitutional Court. For over a decade, the Commission has closely monitored the measures taken by the Hungarian Government. 1.
Why is the Commission silent now when a government is blatantly violating European constitutional principles?
Does the Commission not consider these changes to be contrary to basic democratic principles?

Supporters (2) (11 September 2026) The Commission is aware of the constitutional amendment adopted by the Hungarian National Assembly on 13 July 2026 and signed by the former President of the Republic. The Commission will continue to closely monitor the situation in Hungary, in the overall context of Hungary’s reform efforts to restore the rule of law. The Commission will take into consideration any upcoming Opinion from the Venice Commission of the Council of Europe.
